The study titled Estimates of levels of preterm birth in 2014: a systematic review and modelling analysis, published in The Lancet Global Health in 2019 (Volume 7, Issue 1, Pages e37–e46), provides a comprehensive analysis of preterm birth rates globally for the year 2014. The research employs systematic review methodologies and advanced modeling techniques to estimate the prevalence of preterm births across various regions and populations. 2. The article by Anindya K, Marthias T, Vellakkal S, Carvalho N, Atun R, Morgan A, et al., titled Socioeconomic inequalities in effective service coverage for reproductive, maternal, newborn, and child health: a comparative analysis of 39 low-income and middle-income countries, was published in EClinicalMedicine in 2021 (Volume 40, Article 101103). This study investigates disparities in access to and quality of healthcare services related to reproductive, maternal, newborn, and child health across 39 countries with low and middle incomes. The findings highlight significant socioeconomic inequalities in healthcare service coverage and effectiveness. 3. The research conducted by Arsenault C, Jordan K, Lee D, Dinsa G, Manzi F, Marchant T, et al., titled Equity in antenatal care quality: an analysis of 91 national household surveys, was published in The Lancet Global Health in 2018 (Volume 6, Issue 11, Pages e1186–e1195). This study examines the quality of antenatal care services across 91 countries, focusing on equity in service delivery. The analysis reveals disparities in antenatal care quality, emphasizing the need for targeted interventions to address inequities in maternal healthcare.
